data.description:
## Symptom

EVERY rebar invocation that writes (and reads that reach _store/push.py) under sustained multi-writer load logs 'WARNING rebar.llm.enrich_drain: enrich drain gate check took N ms (> 20 ms budget)' with N observed 339-3589ms on a 5247-ticket store — a permanent, warned-on-every-command steady state.

## Mechanism (proven during /rebar-debug of 3d57-602f-0b75-48ee — see its RCA comment)

maybe_drain runs on the store write path (src/rebar/_store/event_append.py:398, src/rebar/_store/push.py:594) and calls queue.pending_enrichment (src/rebar/llm/overlap/queue.py:414). The O(1) gate marker (task 4144-75d3) is cleared by EVERY queue append, so under sustained concurrent writes the fast path never engages and every command pays a full queue scan. The 20ms budget (llm/config.py, overlap_drain_gate_budget_ms) was calibrated for the marker fast path, not for the full-scan fallback at this store size; the warning itself is by-design observability ('budget is an observed target, not a cutoff', enrich_drain.py:379-385).

## Decision needed (why this is not folded into 3d57's fix)

Fixing this means changing the enrich-drain gate contract — e.g. a marker that tolerates appends (per-ticket dirty set instead of all-or-nothing clear), a store-size-scaled budget, or throttling the warning. That is a design decision on the gate's freshness/latency trade-off, out of scope for the show-stall regression fix.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A recorded decision on the gate contract: append-tolerant marker, recalibrated budget, or throttled warning (with rationale).
- [ ] Under a 10+-concurrent-writer load on a 5000+-ticket store, the gate check either meets its (possibly recalibrated) budget or warns at a bounded, non-per-command rate.
data.title: enrich-drain gate check runs 17-180x over its 20ms budget in steady state under sustained write load
